Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

At the top, include the customer's name, best phone number, and email address, with a note that email is optional. Add the date the order is placed, the requested pickup date, and a pickup time. We are open Tuesday through Sunday, from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. for pickups. A customer should be able to enter a preferred time, but the form should not make it sound like that time is already confirmed. Leave a staff-only space to write the confirmed pickup time after checking the calendar. There should also be a place for the staff member who took the order to put their initials.

For the order itself, provide space for the product name, quantity, size or serving count, and price. Cake orders need a line for flavor, filling, frosting, and a short description of decoration. We offer 6-inch, 8-inch, and 10-inch round cakes, as well as quarter-sheet and half-sheet cakes. The form can list those choices, but it should leave room for a different size to be requested. If a customer asks for writing on a cake, provide a box for the exact wording, and label it so staff know to copy the customer's wording rather than correct it. If no writing is requested, leave that box blank rather than filling it with a dash.

The form also needs to distinguish between requests we can plan for and things that are confirmed. A customer can request a color or a particular style, but that doesn't mean we have promised it. Please include a notes field for those requests and a separate staff field for whether the bakery can accommodate them. One customer recently said, "simple flowers, nothing too tall," and another asked for a blue cake but said, "any shade is fine." Those are useful examples of how customers may describe decoration, but don't print the examples on the form. Keep the fields general enough for other requests too.

1. Put allergy information in a prominent section, separate from decoration notes. Ask the customer to list any allergy or dietary concern, and include a checkbox for "No allergy or dietary concerns reported." If a concern is listed, staff should not treat the checkbox as checked. The form should direct staff to review the concern with the baker before confirming the order. We use shared equipment, so the form must not imply that we can guarantee an allergen-free product. For a phone order, staff should write the customer's words as closely as possible and read them back before ending the call.

2. Include a payment section that records the quoted total, deposit received, remaining balance, and payment method. We accept cash and card in the shop, and customers may pay the full amount when ordering or pay a deposit. A deposit is $10 for orders under $50 and 25 percent of the quoted total for orders of $50 or more. If the order total changes after the customer approves a change, staff should update the quoted total and remaining balance; otherwise, they should leave those amounts as originally recorded. Please give staff a place to note the date a deposit was received, since it may not be the same as the date the form was first filled out.

Some orders change after they are placed, especially decoration details or the number of items in a pastry tray. Include a change log with the date, the requested change, the staff member who discussed it, and whether the customer approved any change in price. Do not make the form suggest that a requested change is accepted just because it has been written down. If a change affects the price, staff should tell the customer the revised amount and record whether the customer approved it. If the customer does not approve the revised price, keep the original order details and mark the change as not approved, rather than replacing the original details.

For timing, we need to know whether an order is routine or needs a short lead time. Customers should be asked to submit cake orders at least 48 hours before pickup and pastry tray orders at least 24 hours before pickup. Bread orders can be placed by 2 p.m. on the day before pickup. If an order arrives later than the relevant cutoff, staff should check with the baker before saying it can be made; if the baker cannot take it, staff should record that it was not accepted, rather than entering it as a confirmed order. This matters because the printed pickup date alone could otherwise look like a promise. Include a space to record the baker's response and the time staff checked.

Please make the form workable on paper and as a fillable digital file. On paper, there should be enough writing room for an order with more than one product, and staff should be able to attach a second page without losing the customer's name or pickup date. For the digital version, use checkboxes only where more than one choice is genuinely available, and keep the fields for written descriptions open for typing. We sometimes receive phone orders while the counter is busy, so avoid tiny labels or a layout that requires staff to jump between distant sections to find the pickup details and payment information.

At the bottom, add a space for the customer to confirm the order details and a separate staff check that the pickup date and time were reviewed against the calendar. Do not label the customer's confirmation as proof that the bakery has accepted a late order; acceptance still depends on the baker's response when a cutoff has passed. Include a final space for staff to note any follow-up that is still needed, such as calling the customer back about a decoration request.
